SMTO-SKL-0037 — SMTO couldn't find that file in Google Drive

GUID: e53e1e3d-d6ce-56fa-898a-9ccf8c01dcb1
Slug: google-drive-file-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google Drive says the file doesn't exist for the account SMTO used. It may have been deleted, moved to a place this account can't see, or belong to a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Drive in your browser with the account SMTO used, and search for the file. Check Trash as well. This shows whether the file was deleted or simply isn't visible to that account.
  2. If the file belongs to a different Google account, tell SMTO to use that account. Each account sees only its own files and the files shared with it.
  3. Ask SMTO to search Drive for the file and pick the exact one from the results before doing anything else with it. Choosing from a fresh search avoids acting on a similar file by mistake.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the file's details, and they match the file you see in Google Drive.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to use "any file with that name" instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 404 or 410 for a file-scoped request using the supplied file_id under the selected account.

What this means

  • Google returns file-scoped HTTP 404 or 410. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns file-scoped HTTP 404 or 410.

How to diagnose it

  • Check account, file_id and provider visibility without assuming the file was deleted.

How to fix it

  • provider_error mapped a 404/410 on a file resource to file_not_found. Verify the exact file_id, the selected account_ref and that account's access in Drive (for example with google_drive.search or google_drive.info under the intended account); never substitute a file chosen by name.
  • Verify the exact file_id, selected account and provider access; do not guess by filename.

Retry and execution caution

  • Verify the exact file_id, selected account and provider access; do not guess by filename.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended file can be read under the authorized account.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
